whyStrictEquivalenceIsNotYetProved.fact: A single initial superset SELECT must materialize document/progress before sweep terminal/revocation decisions, whereas original first query only requests state/revoked. Deferring Java JSON parsing preserves malformed-JSON/type error order but does not preserve SQL projection/column-permission/TOAST/materialization failure order for true denial or missing/terminal branches. Standalone existing APIs must not acquire those extra reads.

The injectable authorization interface does not contractually prohibit same-transaction owner mutations. Current configured implementation is pure, but a supplied callback can access the same physical transaction. Row lock prevents other transactions, not the current transaction. Reusing document/progress captured before callbacks could differ from original fresh repository.lock after callbacks. No actual accepted DB counterexample is claimed; the general source equivalence premise is unproved.
